body:
Tosin Eniolorunda is a Nigerian software engineer and entrepreneur, the co-founder and group chief executive of the financial technology company Moniepoint. He started the business as TeamApt in 2015 with Felix Ike, and it has since grown into a banking and payments network that investors valued as a unicorn in 2024.

Why he is in the news

Moniepoint reached unicorn status after a US$110 million investment in 2024 and raised a further US$200 million in October 2025, which brought attention to its chief executive. Profiles describe him as unusually hands-on with product, and the company's own story is told largely through his decisions.

Early career

Public profiles say he grew up in Ibadan, was apprenticed at an electronics workshop at 16, and studied mechanical engineering at Obafemi Awolowo University. After university he worked as a software engineer at Interswitch, one of Nigeria's major payments companies, where he saw how banks bought and ran payment software.

Building the company

  • 2015: He co-founds TeamApt to build software for banks.
  • 2019: The business gets an agency banking licence and introduces Moniepoint as a mobile-money agent network.
  • 2020: POS terminals are added for agents and merchants.
  • 2022: A business banking licence follows.

See our explainer on Moniepoint for how those products work.

What this profile leaves out

We have deliberately left out family details, date of birth and net worth. They are not needed to understand his work and we have not verified them to our standard.

Sources used

Facts above come from Wikipedia entries, Nairametrics and speaker and company profiles listed below. Where those differ, we have used the more conservative statement.
